headline: Securing Your Stay in Canada's First Interprovincial Park
reservation: Entry permits are required for all vehicles and differ between the Alberta and Saskatchewan sides of the park. While day-use access is generally available at the gate, peak season camping and roofed accommodations often book out months in advance through separate provincial systems. Visitors must verify current requirements on the respective Alberta Parks and Saskatchewan Provincial Parks portals as cross-border pass recognition policies can change.

days.title: High Elevation Pine Forests

stops.name: Horseshoe Canyon Viewpoint
stops.detail: Overlook the dramatic shift from the fescue prairie to the lodgepole pine forests at the park's highest elevations.

stops.name: Firerock Loop
stops.detail: Walk through the unique montane ecosystem that survived the last glacial period, offering a distinct climate from the surrounding plains.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the plateau traverse; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: The West Block is more rugged and may require higher clearance vehicles depending on recent rainfall.

days.title: Centre Block Explorations

stops.name: Loch Leven
stops.detail: Visit the heart of the Saskatchewan side for lakeside trails and a central hub for park information.

stops.name: Conglomerate Cliffs
stops.detail: Observe the rare geological formations composed of rounded river stone cemented together, providing sweeping views of the Adams Creek Valley.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes between the main gate and the cliffs; gravel roads are common.
days.note: Keep an eye on the horizon for sudden prairie storms which can affect road safety.

days.title: Dark Sky and History
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Fort Walsh National Historic Site
stops.detail: Explore the reconstructed NWMP fort to understand the region's complex 19th-century history and the Cypress Hills Massacre.

stops.name: Bald Butte
stops.detail: Climb one of the highest points in the park for a 360-degree panorama of the Cypress Hills plateau.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the round trip to Fort Walsh; watch for free-roaming cattle.
days.note: Fort Walsh operates on a specific seasonal schedule separate from general park access.

intel.title: Dual Jurisdiction
intel.text: The park is split into the West Block and Centre Block, which are not directly connected by internal paved roads. Traveling between them often requires exiting the park and using provincial highways.

intel.title: Gateway Services
intel.text: Fuel is available in Elkwater and Maple Creek, but is limited within the park's interior blocks. Ensure your tank is full before heading to the remote West Block or Fort Walsh.

intel.title: Cellular Gaps
intel.text: Reception is reliable in the townsite of Elkwater and near Loch Leven, but drops significantly in the canyons. Download offline maps for any navigation in the backcountry areas.

intel.title: Dark Sky Preserve
intel.text: As a designated Dark Sky Preserve, lighting is restricted after sunset to protect the nocturnal environment. Plan your return to camp before dusk if you are uncomfortable driving on winding, unlit roads.

intel.title: Viewpoint Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at popular spots like the Conglomerate Cliffs are small and can reach capacity on summer weekends. Arriving before mid-morning is suggested during the July and August peak.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental in Medicine Hat, stock up on supplies at local supermarkets, and allow two hours to reach the Elkwater or Maple Creek park entrances.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for the Centre Block, but an SUV is recommended for the West Block's gravel tracks; check rental agreements for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The Conglomerate Cliffs offer a striking perspective at sunset, though shadows deepen early in the valley.
